name: Bog Kraken
body:
Bog Kraken
CR 19

A towering, tentacled spire of death rises from the murky swamp, covered in bony growths, lichen and moss. Its horrid maw opens and you see no end to the rows of its terrible teeth.

XP 204,800
NE Gargantuan magical beast (aquatic)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 120 ft., low-light vision; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 37, touch 6, flat-footed 37 (+31 natural, -4 size)
hp 350 (20d10+240)
Fort +23, Ref +12, Will +11
DR 10/magic and piercing; Immune disease, mind-affecting effects, poison; Resist acid 30, fire 30

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee bite +32 (6d10+15/19-20 plus grab), 8 tentacles +27 (2d6+7/19-20 plus grab)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft. (40 ft. with tentacles)
Special Attacks biting tentacles, constrict (tentacles, 2d6+15), entrancing lure, swallow whole (special, AC 25, 35 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 40, Dex 10, Con 33, Int 4, Wis 16, Cha 9
Base Atk +20; CMB +39 (+43 grapple); CMD 49 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Blind-Fight, Critical Focus, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Perception, Stealth), Toughness, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Perception +16, Stealth +8, Swim +27; Racial Modifiers +8 Stealth
Languages Aquan, Common (can’t speak)
SQ amphibious, tenacious grapple

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Biting Tentacles (Ex)

Bog kraken’s tentacles end with secondary mouths consisting of four flaps lined with teeth. The tentacle attacks of a bog kraken count as a bite for all advantageous purposes (like the weapon focus feat) and deal bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage.

Entrancing Lure (Su)

Each of bog kraken’s tentacles is equipped with a dangling, glowing bulb not unlike an anglerfish’s lure. When the bog kraken succeeds at a grapple check to start or maintain the grapple with its tentacle, the grappled creature has to succeed at a DC 31 Will save or be dazed for 1 round. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Obliterating Bite (Ex)

A creature swallowed whole by the bog kraken automatically takes 24d10+60 damage, as if hit by a critical hit from its bite with a x4 multiplier. This damage ignores hardness and damage reduction. If the creature is brought below 50% of its maximum hit points by this damage, it has to succeed at a DC 35 Fortitude save or die as if it was a victim of a coup de grace attempt. If the creature dies, it has to succeed at a DC 35 Fortitude save or its body and equipment are utterly destroyed. Only true resurrection can bring such a victim back to life, and only artifacts and other items immune to conventional damage may be recovered from the slain beast’s innards. The save DCs are Strength-based.

Tenacious Grapple (Ex)

A bog kraken does not gain the grappled condition if it grapples a foe.

ECOLOGY

Environment any swamp
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

While the great and mysterious krakens of the vast oceans are widely known in sailor legends, not many know of the bog krakens. Not many of those beasts exist and the reason for their existence is not entirely understood. The most common version says that the bog krakens evolved from krakens trapped in shallow, inland waters after ancient, apocalyptic events and over years and generations these tenacious beings mutated to better adapt to this new habitat. Some people believe that this creature is only distantly, if at all, related to the famous, cunning sea monsters.

Regardless of their history, the bog krakens differ quite a bit from their oceanic cousins. First, the bog krakens are devoid of higher intellect, barely having enough to understand basic language and lay cunning ambushes. This remnant of genius, along with their magically entrancing lures, is what allows the bog krakens to occasionally gather small, isolated sects of followers, who unwittingly start to gather and build communities in the swamp, until the beast finds its little herd big enough for a feast.

With the intellect also went the awesome magical powers of the krakens. They adapted, of course, by becoming monstrously strong and deadly combatants, overwhelmingly physically powerful in comparison to krakens of deeper waters. Mostly stationary in shallow swamps, the bog krakens are amphibious and possess secondary mouths on their tentacles that allow them to more efficiently attack, kill and devour prey when catching and throwing it into their vast, cavernous maw is not feasible. Despite its eight tentacles being highly advanced, a bog kraken does not have the longer arms of the normal kraken, as those have atrophied to little stumps capable only of making sure that the food lands between rows upon rows of sharp teeth lining its mouth. The head of the bog kraken is enormous and heavily armored in bony plates that turn aside blows and slashes, leaving sharp, piercing weapons most suitable for the task of slaying the beast.

A bog kraken is a terrifying monstrosity, especially against unprepared enemies. Landing in one of its tentacles is often a death sentence, as the lure keeps most victims still when the appendage crushes and tears at them. It is the maw, though, that’s the most terrifying, as once it clenches shut on a victim, it thoroughly delimbs and destroys whatever fell inside, leaving it without a real chance of survival. Before you stands what seems to be an enormous bull made entirely of jagged, volcanic stone. Its tail is long and covered in spikes, and its head is devoid of any features, except for a pair of monstrous, beetle-like mandibles.
